title: Bumrah Returns to India Squad for Afghanistan T20I Series, Subject to Fitness Clearance
excerpt: India's pace spearhead is back in the 15-member squad for the three-match T20I series in New Delhi, with Shreyas Iyer captaining and teenager Vaibhav Sooryavanshi earning a call-up.
body:
• Jasprit Bumrah has been named in India's squad for the three-match T20I series against Afghanistan, subject to fitness clearance, after missing the Sri Lanka Test series due to an impact injury sustained during the England tour.
  • Shreyas Iyer will captain the side with Tilak Varma as vice-captain, while Sanju Samson returns and teenager Vaibhav Sooryavanshi earns a call-up after two half-centuries against Zimbabwe.
  • World Cup-winning skipper Suryakumar Yadav has been left out again, and Hardik Pandya has not been included despite media speculation.
  • All three matches will be played at Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi on September 13, 15, and 17.

Bumrah Back in the Fold After Injury Layoff

India's pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah has been named in a 15-member squad for the three-match T20I series against Afghanistan, the BCCI announced on Monday, though his inclusion is subject to fitness clearance.

Bumrah last played for India on July 16 against England at Sophia Gardens, Cardiff, where he sustained an impact injury while fielding. He was subsequently ruled out of the final ODI at Lord's and missed India's entire Test series against Sri Lanka, which India won 1-0.

Fast bowlers Harshit Rana and all-rounders Nitish Kumar Reddy and Washington Sundar have also been picked subject to fitness, signalling the selectors' intent to rebuild the pace and all-round stocks ahead of the ODI World Cup cycle.

Iyer Leads, Sooryavanshi Gets the Nod

Shreyas Iyer will captain the squad with Tilak Varma serving as vice-captain. The leadership pair reflects the BCCI's continued investment in a post-Rohit Sharma transition for the shortest format, with both players having impressed in recent bilateral series.

Wicketkeeper-batter Sanju Samson has been recalled after missing India's T20I series against Zimbabwe, while teenager Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has been rewarded with a squad berth following two half-centuries in that tour. The 18-year-old left-hander adds a dynamic option at the top of the order alongside Abhishek Sharma.

"The selectors have gone with a strong, balanced squad that combines experience with exciting young talent."

— BCCI statement

The top order shapes up as Sooryavanshi, Abhishek Sharma, Samson, and Ishan Kishan, with Iyer and Tilak Varma anchoring the middle order. Shivam Dube provides the left-handed hitting option lower down.

Notable Absences

World Cup-winning captain Suryakumar Yadav has been left out of the squad once again, extending his absence from T20I duty despite being India's highest-ranked T20I batter. No official reason has been provided for his continued omission.

Hardik Pandya, whose name had been floated in media reports, has not been included either. Eight players from the Zimbabwe squad have been dropped, including Rinku Singh, Mayank Yadav, Prince Yadav, Suryansh Shedge, Harsh Dubey, Prabhsimran Singh, Yash Thakur, and Ashok Sharma.

Spin-Heavy Attack With Pace Firepower

The bowling attack pairs Bumrah and Arshdeep Singh as the lead seamers, with Harshit Rana adding express pace. The spin department features Varun Chakaravarthy and Ravi Bishnoi as wrist-spin options, while Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, and Nitish Reddy offer left-arm orthodox, off-spin, and seam-bowling all-round depth respectively.

The balance of the squad suggests India are preparing for conditions at Arun Jaitley Stadium, where pitches in September typically offer assistance to slower bowlers in the evening sessions.

Series Details and Looking Ahead

All three T20Is will be played at Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi on September 13, 15, and 17. Afghanistan, who host their home fixtures in India under the ICC's Future Tours Program, will be looking to build on their competitive showings in recent bilateral series.

For India, the series represents a crucial checkpoint in their white-ball rebuild. Bumrah's fitness will be monitored closely — his death-overs bowling remains arguably the most valuable asset in world cricket, and the team management will want to ensure he is fully fit before the busier schedule ahead.

The series also gives the selectors a window to assess their options for the 2027 ODI World Cup, with several squad positions still up for grabs across formats.
